title: Flip batches on an assembly line
prompt:
head is an assembly line stored as a singly linked list; reverse each consecutive batch of k nodes in place, leave a final batch shorter than k as it is, and return the new head.

- Each node is an object with val (an integer) and next (the next node or null; None in Python). In Python, nodes are dicts: node["val"], node["next"].
- The list has 0 to 300 nodes; 1 <= k <= 300 (if k exceeds the length, nothing changes).
- Relink the existing nodes with O(1) extra space (no recursion or arrays of nodes).
hints: Before reversing a batch, make sure k nodes are actually left. How do you check that without losing your place?
Track before, the node just ahead of the current batch (a dummy at first). Probe k steps from before; if you fall off the end, stop.
Reverse the batch by repeatedly moving start.next to just after before (k - 1 moves). Then start is the batch's last node and becomes the next before.

solution.explanation: A dummy node and a before pointer mark where each batch attaches. A k-step probe confirms a full batch exists; head-insertion then reverses it in place, and the batch's original first node, now last, becomes the anchor for the next batch.

complexity.notes: Each node is probed once and moved at most once, so the work is linear despite the nested loops.

followUps: Also reverse the final short batch.
Reverse only every other batch of k nodes.
